title: Learnings from Healthcare Systems with Large Reductions in Cancer Mortality: A Rapid Evidence Summary
content: In Wales, cancer is responsible for more than one in four deaths. The incidence of cancer is on the rise and it is projected that by 2035, there will be approximately 24,000 new cancer cases each year in Wales compared to approximately 20,000 in 2019. A new 10-year National Cancer Strategy for Wales will be announced in February 2027. This document was produced to gather learnings from other countries that have achieved improved cancer outcomes in recent years, to support the development of the strategy.The aim of this rapid evidence summary was to identify and describe structures and processes implemented at a national or regional level in countries that have significantly improved cancer outcomes in recent years.This rapid evidence summary consists of two parts. The first part summarised published evidence that directly linked cancer outcomes to country-level factors. Systematic searches of multiple academic and grey literature databases as well as supplementary searches were used to identify such evidence. The second part of this document reported learnings from countries with large reductions in mortality. Targeted searches for country-specific evidence were performed. Findings were summarised narratively.This rapid evidence summary identified only two studies linking relevant country-level factors, including healthcare system characteristics and characteristics of countries’ cancer plans and strategies, to cancer outcomes. To support the development of the new 10-year National Cancer Strategy for Wales, learnings from countries that have seen large improvements in cancer mortality over the recent years have been identified and summarised. While it is difficult to directly link improvements in cancer outcomes in a country to national cancer plans, we hope that examples of cancer-related activities in a wide range of countries that have successfully reduced mortality will provide useful learnings. Due to the high variation in the country contexts, considerations about the applicability to Wales need to be made. In the report, we also discuss the policy and practice implications of the findings, and the research implications and evidence gaps.
